content.text:
I reviewed every input file, every draft section, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs, and built a full limitation-by-limitation source ledger against the disclosure (the only USER-authored technical authority, with `input/conversation.md` duplicating it in truncated form).

**Ledger highlights (all traced):** rail/flat lower face/upper face/longitudinal slot/printed distance marks; fence at first end, perpendicular, downwardly projecting portion bearing the edge, two screws in two corresponding holes, inversion moving the portion between longitudinal sides, same marked face reused; removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces changing setback without changing separation; two separate carriages, keys in the slot preventing rotation while permitting sliding; one cylindrical bushing per carriage with a bore through the carriage registering with the slot, bores parallel and perpendicular to the lower face; clamp knob above the rail with a threaded shank through carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below, tightening clamping the rail, loosening releasing; two pointers aligned with their bore axes readable against the same marks, difference = center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the midpoint and shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with it and with a pencil centerline; the full use sequence; materials (rigid polymer or metal, hardened-metal replaceable bushings); and the no-motor/battery/sensor/network negatives. Claims 1–22, including every dependent limitation, map onto those passages; the abstract is 149 words; §1.83(a) drawing coverage of claimed features is complete.

**Consistency checks:** each of the 27 numerals has exactly one referent, appears in at least one figure brief, and every parenthetical figure cite in the description matches that figure's numeral list. Section lines 3-3 and 5-5 carry the same designation in FIG. 2, in the FIG. 3/FIG. 5 briefs, and in the Brief Description, and the carriage each section passes through (70 for 3-3, 50 for 5-5) agrees across all three places. No placeholders, drafting notes, or unresolved alternatives remain, and the schematic-depiction language ("shown schematically", plain block/round body/rectangular body) is confined to the figure briefs — the specification never justifies a renderer's outline with "by way of example" or "any closed outline".

One note for your awareness, not a finding against the draft: the disclosure itself is geometrically ambiguous about whether the rail sits parallel to the referenced edge (which the figure briefs depict, and which the fence-lip-on-a-longitudinal-side and common-setback language implies) or perpendicular to it ("the rail extends inward across the workpiece"). The draft reproduces the inventor's wording verbatim in both places rather than resolving it, so there is nothing untraced to remove; the FIG. 7 centerline statement likewise repeats the source's own "align the center index and the sight notch with a pencil centerline" without adding a direction. Also, the prior-art search was not run, so the Background characterizations rest on whatever is in `prior_art/` and may be incomplete — that art is traced by a later review, not this one.

input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed on the whole candidate: all 22 claims (independent 1, 13, 18 and every dependent limitation), all 27 reference numerals and numbered parts, all seven figure briefs plus the Brief Description of Drawings, the title, field, background, summary, detailed description, and abstract were checked and individually traced to affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md (input/conversation.md is the same text, truncated, and adds nothing). Every technical element traces: elongated straight rail with flat lower face, upper face, straight longitudinal slot through the rail, printed distance marks beside the slot; fixed fence at the first end, perpendicular to the rail, downwardly projecting portion bearing on the workpiece edge, releasable mounting by two screws in two corresponding holes, inversion moving the projecting portion from one longitudinal side to the opposite side while the same marked face and reading direction are reused; removable spacer plate with parallel opposite faces changing setback by its thickness without changing separation; two separate guide carriages on the upper face, each with a lower key in the slot preventing rotation while permitting sliding, one cylindrical drill bushing whose bore passes completely through the carriage and registers with the slot, bores parallel and perpendicular to the flat lower face; threaded clamp knob above the rail whose shank passes through carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below, tightening clamping the rail between carriage and shoe and loosening permitting sliding; first and second pointers aligned with their bore axes and readable against the same distance marks with the difference equal to center-to-center hole spacing; transverse center index at the rail midpoint and shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with it and alignable with a pencil centerline; the complete use sequence (select spacing, loosen, slide to readings centered about the index, tighten, place, press fence or spacer against the edge, align, drill both bushings, lift away with nothing left attached); materials of rigid polymer or metal with hardened-metal replaceable bushings; and the no-motor, no-battery, no-sensor, no-network negatives. Internal consistency was verified: each numeral has a single referent, appears in at least one figure brief, and every parenthetical figure citation in the description matches that figure's numeral list; section lines 3-3 and 5-5 carry the same designation in the FIG. 2 source-view brief, in the FIG. 3 and FIG. 5 resulting-view briefs, and in the drawing description, and the carriage sectioned by each line (70 for 3-3, 50 for 5-5) agrees in all three places; claims and description use identical relationships and terminology (rail, fixed fence, guide carriage, drill bushing, clamp knob, clamping shoe, spacer plate, pointer, center index, sight notch all preserved); antecedent bases are intact; the abstract is 149 words; and every feature recited in the claims is shown in a figure. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains. Schematic depiction language (plain block, plain round body, plain rectangular body, straight elongated opening) is confined to the figure briefs, is used only for parts the inventor affirmatively disclosed, adds no undisclosed depth, taper, angle, runout, contact topology, proportion, or count, and is never echoed into the specification as an example embodiment or "any outline" broadening statement. Two contextual notes that are not findings: the disclosure itself leaves the rail-to-edge orientation ambiguous (fence perpendicular to the rail and the rail extending inward across the workpiece versus the lip on a longitudinal side implying a rail parallel to the edge), and the draft reproduces the inventor's wording verbatim rather than resolving it, so there is no untraced assertion to remove; and no prior-art search was run, so the Background characterizations rest on whatever is in prior_art/ and may be incomplete, which a later review traces. No unsupported technical assertion or verified internal inconsistency was found.
